reasons: Classification is correct: the Agreement auto-renews for successive 1-year terms (term length fine), but the only post-Initial-Term exit requires ninety (90) days' notice, which exceeds the fallback ceiling of a 60-day non-renewal/notice window while stopping short of walk-away territory — a genuine deviation on a material term.

The redline is directionally right and actionable: it cuts Customer's for-convenience/non-renewal notice to thirty (30) days (preferred position) and expressly ties it to electing not to renew, while leaving Kubient at ninety days, which favours our side and is permissible under the 'do not flag/degrade terms that benefit our party' principle.

The rewrite touches only the one operative sentence; the 0.623 changed-character ratio is an artefact of the sentence being restructured into party-specific limbs and is justified because a symmetric 90-day sentence cannot be fixed with a smaller edit.
Comment is accurate, uses the [Playbook] prefix and first person plural, states what changed and why, cites the position, and offers the 60-day fallback without lecturing.
The absence of renewal price-uplift language is correctly noted as not engaged rather than being flagged as a separate deviation.
